Pinned-source conventions: work over the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A category fibred in groupoids is represented by an algebraic space $F$ over $S$ if it is equivalent over the site to $\mathcal S_F$, the category fibred in sets associated to the functor of points of $F$. A fibred category is fibred in setoids when its fibre categories are groupoids and all their objects have trivial automorphism groups. For a presheaf $F$ of sets, $\mathcal S_F$ is its associated category fibred in sets: its objects over $T$ are elements of $F(T)$. A 1-morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of categories fibred in groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces when for EVERY scheme $U$ over $S$ and every $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, the 2-fibre product $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space over $U$.

Let $S$ be a scheme in the big fppf site, and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Then $\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space over $S$ if and only if (i) every object in every fibre groupoid $\mathcal X_U$ has trivial automorphism group and (ii) the presheaf of sets $U\mapsto\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X_U)/\cong$ is represented by an algebraic space over $S$.

conclusions: Representability of $\mathcal X$ by an algebraic space is equivalent to the conjunction of (i) trivial automorphisms in every fibre and (ii) representability by an algebraic space of the presheaf of isomorphism classes.
